This 1942 airmail cover from Pearl Harbor, T.H. went through that system: its title notes the censor marking I.C.B. Censor 4. Postal history you can hold in one hand.

fact: Hawaii stayed under martial law for almost three years, until October 24, 1944.

title_at_writing: Scott #253 US 1894 3c Jackson Purple First Bureau Issue Unwatermarked Used
story: Until 1894, private companies printed every U.S. postage stamp under contract with the Post Office. That July the Bureau of Engraving and Printing took over the job from the American Bank Note Company, and the stamps of those first years are known as the First Bureau Issue. Andrew Jackson, the seventh president, earned the nickname Old Hickory by sharing his soldiers' hardships, and here he is on the 3c, purple, unwatermarked and used, just as the title says. A handsome souvenir of the year Uncle Sam started printing his own.
headline: The first stamps Uncle Sam printed
hook: In 1894 the Bureau of Engraving and Printing took over U.S. stamps, and Jackson got the 3c.
fact: In 1833 Jackson dismissed his Treasury secretary, William J. Duane, for refusing to move the government's deposits out of the Second Bank of the United States. Duane's story is on this site too.

title_at_writing: Scott #RD125 US Series 1942 50c Stock Transfer Duane Green Full Perfin Used
story: In May 1833 Andrew Jackson made William J. Duane his Secretary of the Treasury, then told him to move the government's money out of the Second Bank of the United States. Duane refused to act without the consent of Congress, and that September Jackson dismissed him after only four months in the job. Roger B. Taney took over and moved the deposits to state banks. Here is Duane again on a 1942 series 50c stock transfer stamp in green, with a full perfin: small holes punched in a pattern, usually a firm's initials. Holes and all, he still looks like a man who would not back down.
headline: The secretary who said no
hook: Andrew Jackson dismissed his Treasury secretary after four months for saying no.
fact: The Senate censured Jackson in March 1834, and Henry Clay's first draft named the firing of Duane. The censure was expunged in 1837.

title_at_writing: Scott #OL3-OL5 Germany Prussia 1903 Frei Durch Ablösung Nr.21 Official Set MH
story: Frei durch Ablösung means, roughly, free by settlement: Prussia's state offices did not pay postage letter by letter, because their mail was covered by a lump-sum contract with the German Reichspost. In 1903 the officials had to put these stamps on their mail anyway, for one year only, so the true amount of official mail could be counted and the payment set again. The Nr. 21 is Prussia's contract number, in force since April 1, 1894. A tidy official set from 1903, MH, just as the title says. Willkommen to the album.
headline: Stamps that counted the mail
hook: Prussia paid its official postage in one lump sum. In 1903 these stamps counted the letters.
fact: The count found far less official mail than the Reichspost had assumed, so the payments were cut. Baden ran the same count in 1905, with its own Nr. 16.

title_at_writing: Scott #R160-R168 (Used) 1898 Battleship Revenue Handstamp 1/8c to 5c Lot of 11
story: In February 1898 the U.S. battleship Maine exploded and sank in Havana harbor, and that April Congress voted to go to war with Spain. To pay the bills, Congress passed an act to meet war expenditures, signed on June 13, 1898, and soon known as the War Revenue Act. It taxed tobacco, sugar refining and sales on the exchanges, and it required tax stamps on business papers such as bills of lading and sale memos. This used lot of 11 Battleship revenues from 1898 runs from 1/8c to 5c, handstamps and all, as the title says. A small fleet, still on duty in your album.
headline: A fleet of war-tax stamps
hook: In 1898 Congress paid for a war with Spain partly through stamps on everyday paperwork.
fact: The same 1898 act brought the first federal tax on telephone service: 1 cent on long-distance calls, until it was repealed in 1902.

title_at_writing: Scott #231 1893 2c Columbian Exposition Landing of Columbus MINT Single Stamp
story: Chicago's 1893 World's Columbian Exposition celebrated the 400th anniversary of Columbus's 1492 landing, and the Post Office Department joined in with the nation's first commemorative stamps, the Columbians. The 2c design is based on John Vanderlyn's painting Landing of Columbus, which Congress commissioned in 1836 for the Capitol Rotunda. Two cents paid the domestic first-class rate, and 72 percent of the more than two billion Columbians issued were 2c stamps. This 1893 2c Landing of Columbus is a mint single, just as the title says. Columbus has landed in your album, beard and all.
headline: A Capitol painting goes postal
hook: A painting from the U.S. Capitol became a 2c stamp in America's first commemorative set.
fact: Collectors have long chuckled that the 2c shows Columbus with a beard, while the 1c, set one day earlier, shows him clean-shaven.

title_at_writing: Scott #287 (MH) 1898 4c Indian Hunting Buffalo Trans-Mississippi Orange
story: Inspired by Chicago's 1893 fair, Omaha held its own world's fair in 1898, the Trans-Mississippi Exposition, to promote the development of the Midwest and West. Omaha Daily Bee publisher Edward Rosewater convinced Postmaster General James A. Gary to issue nine stamps for it, and apart from the 1893 Columbians they were the only U.S. commemoratives of the 1800s. The 4c Indian Hunting Buffalo zooms in on the central scene of a larger engraving from an 1854 book on the Indian tribes of the United States. This 1898 4c in orange is MH, just as the title says. More than a century on, the chase is still at full gallop.
headline: Omaha's world's fair buffalo hunt
hook: A buffalo hunt from an 1854 book became a stamp for Omaha's 1898 world's fair.
fact: The 4c was often used to pay the domestic first-class rate on a double-weight letter.

title_at_writing: Scott #328 (MNH) 1907 Jamestown Exposition 1c Captain John Smith Green
story: Jamestown, founded in 1607, became the first permanent English settlement in North America, and in 1907 an exposition at Hampton Roads, near Norfolk, Virginia, marked its 300th anniversary. In 1608 Captain John Smith and several fellow colonists explored 2,500 miles of the Chesapeake Bay and many of its rivers, and that September he was elected president of the colony. His portrait on the 1c was inspired by Simon de Passe's 1616 engraving. This 1907 Jamestown Exposition 1c in green is MNH, just as the title says. Captain Smith still looks ready to chart the next river.
headline: The captain who mapped the Chesapeake
hook: Jamestown turned 300 in 1907, and its best-known captain got the 1c stamp.
fact: The exposition grounds later became Naval Station Norfolk: the Navy bought the land right after the United States entered World War I in April 1917.

title_at_writing: Scott #C47 (MNH) 1953 6c Powered Flight 50th Anniversary Airmail Sheet of 50
story: On December 17, 1903, at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, Orville Wright piloted the brothers' Flyer for 12 seconds and 120 feet, opening the era of controlled, powered flight. Three more flights followed that morning, and the best, with Wilbur at the controls, covered 852 feet in 59 seconds. For the 50th anniversary, a 6c airmail stamp honoring powered flight was issued on May 29, 1953. This 1953 sheet holds 50 of those 6c airmails, MNH, just as the title says. Fifty stamps, all cleared for takeoff.
headline: Twelve seconds over Kitty Hawk
hook: The Wrights' first powered flight lasted 12 seconds, and its 50th birthday got a 6c airmail.
fact: The original 1903 Flyer went on loan to London's Science Museum in 1928, came back to the United States in 1948 and was formally donated to the Smithsonian on December 17, the 45th anniversary of its flights.

title_at_writing: Philippines Scott #425-430 (MNH) 1937 Eucharistic Congress Commonwealth Set of 6
story: From February 3 to 7, 1937, Manila hosted the 33rd International Eucharistic Congress, the first one ever held in the Far East. Pope Pius XI sent Cardinal Dennis Dougherty, archbishop of Philadelphia, as his legate. The islands were then a commonwealth under the 1934 Tydings-McDuffie Act, on a ten-year road to independence that came on July 4, 1946. This 1937 Commonwealth set of 6 is MNH, just as the title says. Six little souvenirs of one very big week in Manila.
headline: Manila's big week of 1937
hook: In 1937 Manila hosted a worldwide Catholic congress, the first in the Far East.
fact: Cardinal Dougherty knew the islands well: he was named a bishop in the Philippines in 1903, and he called his 1937 return a home-coming.

title_at_writing: Scott #2203 (MNH) 1986 Sojourner Truth Black Heritage Sheet of 50 Plate A111111
story: Born Isabella Baumfree around 1797 in Ulster County, New York, she was enslaved until 1826, when she walked away with her infant daughter. Isaac and Maria Van Wagenen took them in at New Paltz, and in 1828 a court ruled in her favor and her son Peter, sold to Alabama against the law, came home. In 1843 she took the name Sojourner Truth and traveled the country speaking against slavery and for women's rights. The Postal Service issued her stamp in New Paltz on February 4, 1986. This Black Heritage sheet of 50, MNH, carries plate A111111, as the title says. Fifty portraits, and she still has the floor.
headline: She walked out and spoke up
hook: She walked to freedom with her baby in 1826, then spent her life speaking up.
fact: In 2009 a bronze bust of her by Artis Lane was unveiled in Emancipation Hall, the first sculpture in the U.S. Capitol to honor an African American woman.

hook: Every stamp on this pane is a Jeopardy! clue, with the response printed upside down.
